faq.q: Why use Grade 12 Ti-0.3Mo-0.8Ni for titanium reactor impeller blade?
faq.a: Grade 12 (Ti-0.3Mo-0.8Ni) offers enhanced high-temperature strength and crevice corrosion resistance in hot chloride environments, ideal for chemical processing equipment and heat exchangers.

faq.q: How is a titanium reactor impeller blade manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium reactor impeller blade is manufactured using Seamless tube extrusion; CNC machining; TIG welding (ERTi-2 filler); Hydrostatic testing. BOZE CNC Ti uses precision CNC equipment with strict process controls to ensure consistent quality and dimensional accuracy.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 12 Ti-0.3Mo-0.8Ni for titanium reactor impeller blade?
faq.a: Alternative materials include stainless steel (heavier, susceptible to corrosion) and aluminum (lower strength, shorter fatigue life). The alternative manufacturing method is Laser welding (higher capital cost, limited wall thickness capability).

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium reactor impeller blade?
faq.a: Titanium Reactor Impeller Blade components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348, ASME. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium reactor impeller blade?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86). BOZE CNC Ti mitigates these through strict process control, proper material selection, and 100% inspection.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for custom titanium reactor impeller blade?
faq.a: Standard lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders can be accommodated. Contact our sales team for specific delivery schedules.
